to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

MARKING OF SERVICING, MAINTENANCE, 

GROUND HANDLING AND SAFETY/HAZARD 

POINTS ON AIRCRAFT 



1. Scope — Specifies the symbols, their positions and sizes to be used for the marking of servicing, 
maintenance, ground handling and safety/hazard points on aircrafts, to enable them to be quickly 
identified during intermediate stops on scheduled flights and during scheduled maintenance checks. 
It also covers the requirements for warning markings to prevent damage to the equipment or injury to 
personnel, and for the marking of hatches. 

1.1 This standard does not cover emergency markings .and the materials to be used for markings. 

2. Servicing, Maintenance, Ground Handling and Safety/Hazard Points 

2.1 Markings 

2.1.1 Servicing, maintenance and ground handling points— Servicing, maintenance and ground 
handling points shall be marked with the symbols described in Table 1 and shown in Fig. 1 and 2, and, 
where applicable, with the additional information given in Table 1. 

The symbols shown in Fig. 1 shall be black on a white background or white on a black 
background. 

The yellow-orange colour of the basic symbols shown in Fig. 2 shall be the IS Colour No. 368 
conforming to IS : 5-1978 'Colours for ready mixed paints and enamels {third revision ) '. 

2.1.2 Safety/ hazard points — Safety/hazard points shall be marked in accordance with Table 2 
and Fig. 3. 

Except where otherwise indicated in Table 2, the markings shall be fluorescent red. 

2.2 Position of Markings— The markings shall be situated on the part concerned, or immediately 
adjacent to it, and on the access panel. When they are concealed, they shall be either accompanied 
or replaced by arrows bearing the same symbol which will assist in locating the markings. 

2.3 Size of Markings 

2.3.1 The size of the markings shall be commensurate with the distance from which they shall 
be visible. 

2.3.2 The warning symbol for explosive-actuated devices (see Table 2) shall be of the largest 
practicable size up to 230 mm sides. Other symbols shall be approximately 100 mm in the longest 
dimension. 

2.3.3 Unless otherwise specified, letters shall be 38 mm high. 

3. Hatches f 

3.1 A hatch giving access to a slicing point shall be outlined by an unbroken line in the appropriate 
basic colour. f- 

3.2 A hatch or panel covering several points shall be marked with all the appropriate basic colours. 
Other written markings may be added, but they shall not replace the individual identifications nor 
interfere with their interpretation.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 



This standard conforms to ISO 1950-1974 Aircraft- Identification of servicing, maintenance, 
ground handling and safety/hazard points, issued by International Organization for Standardization 
(ISO).
